forcedChoices.choice: «antes de que se pronunciara la bendición de despedida»
forcedChoices.reason: The English 'he' can refer to Peter or to Jesus; the impersonal form keeps both readings.
Jesus speaks to the two twins at once, so Spanish needs the plural.
'thereto' can refer to the door or to the kingdom; the form without a pronoun keeps both.

forcedChoices.choice: «Parecía hablar por sí mismo, como quien tiene autoridad»
forcedChoices.reason: 'speak of himself' contrasts with a prophet who declares God's word, so it means on his own authority; 'hablar de sí mismo' would mean 'talk about himself'.
Spanish 'maestro' covers both 'master' and 'teacher', so 'instructor' renders 'teacher'; 'prójimo' carries the sense of 'neighbor' as a fellow man.
